this meeting. To participate in the City of Commerce ‘public meetings and provide public

record.

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS

1.. Presentation/Update from the Sheriff's Department Regarding Public Safety in the City of Commerce Sgt. Villarreal provided an overview of the statistics for the last two weeks.  

2.. Reorganization of City Council Councilmember Argumedo moved, Mayor Mendoza seconded, to nominate and appoint Mayor Pro Tem Rebollo for Mayor for 2022-2023. The motion carried by the following vote: 

YES: Councilmembers Argumedo, Altamirano, Mayor Pro Tem Rebollo and Mayor Mendoza (4)
Absent: Councilmember Soria (1)

Councilmember Mendoza moved, seconded by Mayor Rebollo, to nominate and appoint Councilmember Argumedo for Mayor Pro Tem for 2022-2023. The motion was carried by the following vote: 

AYES: Councilmembers Argumedo, Altamirano, Mendoza and Mayor Rebollo (4)
Absent: Councilmember Soria (1)

Representatives from Supervisor Janice Harn's Office congratulated Mayor Rebollo on her appointment and thanked outgoing Mayor Mendoza for his service as mayor of the City of Commerce during 2021-to 2022. 

Councilmembers and Mayor Rebollo thanked outgoing Mayor Mendoza for his service. 
Councilmember Mendoza talked about his over 30-year residency and community involvement and thanked for the opportunity to serve as a Mayor from 2021-to 2022. 


PUBLIC COMMENT Director of Administrative Services and City Clerk Shumway read thank you letters for outgoing Mayor Mendoza submitted by Maribel Mendoza, Johncito Perraza, Esther Zavala, and Daniel Cortez.

Director of Administrative Services and City Clerk read letter from employees asking for their pay cut given back: David Torres, Jesse Hernandez, and Angela Picazzo-Lopez. 

MaryAnn Griego read letters asking for the employees pay cut given back.

The letter from the Transportation Department  was signed by 27 employees.  Additional letters were submitted by Rachel Baltierra,  Mack Jefferson, Alfredo Beltran, Omar Olivas, Denise Raigosa, Chris Muniz, Fransisco Navarro, Brenda Diaz, MaryAnn Griego, and Kevin Larsen.  Francisco Navarro, Matt  Jefferson, Veronica Diaz, Chris Munoz,  Omar Olivas, Maryann Griego.






CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Ivan Altamirano Councilmember Altamirano commented on item #8. According to Councilmember Altamirano, two Ukrainian refugee families from Ukraine are in the City of Commerce. Councilmember Altamirano thanked Commerce Casino for providing rooms, food, and accommodations for these two families. In addition, Councilmember Altamirano thanked Commerce residents who welcomed refugees and helped them. According to Councilmember Altamirano, the City Council staff is working on finding permanent housing for the refugees and continuing to support those two families. The families, in turn, are incredibly grateful for all the help that they received.

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Mendoza spoke in support of reinstating the pay for the employees. Councilmember Mendoza noted that he has been a union member for many years and agrees that employees should be treated fairly. 

Councilmember Mendoza reported that on March 11, 2022, he met with the Supervisor Janice Hahn, on March 31, 2022, attended a Neighborhood Watch meeting at Bristow Park, on March 12, 2022, attended 14 year -old Crush Volleyball tournament, and on April 3, 2022, delivered State of the City address, on April 6, 2022, attended Tree of Remembrance, and on April 9, 2022, attended Spring Festival. 

Councilmember Mendoza asked that the retirees are invited to all City events. Councilmember Mendoza stated that the Senior Brunch in the Senior Center hosted by the Commerce Casino was a great event that seniors enjoyed. 

Councilmember Altamirano spoke about inflation and asked that the letter is written and sent out to Assembly members and the Governor requesting to remove the significant gas tax that was put in place about three years ago. 

Mayor Pro Tem Argumedo reported that he attended a Neighborhood Watch meeting in Bristow park. Mayor Pro Tem Argumedo agreed that employees need to be treated fairly, and the City will continue working on these issues. 

Mayor Rebollo thanked for being appointed as a Mayor and thanked the community for standing behind her.

Mayor Rebollo requested that a financial workshop is scheduled in order to sit down with the employees and understand the financial situation.
